title: Chapter Nine: Forms and Nature of Literature
subject: GST 111

questions.question: The word literature is derived from the Latin word?
questions.explanation: The word literature is derived from the Latin word 'litera' and Greek word 'literatura'.

questions.question: The Greek word 'literatura' means?
questions.explanation: Both 'litera' and 'literatura' mean 'printed matter'.

questions.question: Literature helps us to discover ourselves and the meaning of?
questions.explanation: Literature can help us to discover ourselves and the meaning of life through universal artists.

questions.question: According to Ezeugo, the best way to talk about literature is by?
questions.explanation: Ezeugo suggests that the best way to talk about literature is by reading texts of literature.

questions.question: Literature is described as an art that improves the awareness, consciousness and?
questions.explanation: Literature is an art that improves the awareness, the consciousness and conscience of a milieu.

questions.question: According to Ezeugo, literature subtly tells what happened to man and what man imagined could have?
questions.explanation: Literature tells what happened to man and what man imagined could have happened to him.

questions.question: One of the major mysteries of man is?
questions.explanation: One of the major mysteries of man is man himself, and literary art is at the centre of that mystery.

questions.question: While science helps man understand his natural environment, literature helps man understand?
questions.explanation: Literature helps man understand himself while science helps him understand his natural environment.

questions.question: Literature is divided into two major parts: fiction and?
questions.explanation: Literature is divided into two major parts — fiction and non-fiction.

questions.question: Fiction deals with events that are not real but are?
questions.explanation: Fiction deals with events that are not real but are imagined.

questions.question: Non-fiction deals with real or factual stories about human?
questions.explanation: Non-fiction deals with real or factual stories about human experiences.

questions.question: Biography and autobiography are special forms of?
questions.explanation: Non-fiction usually takes special forms such as prose — biography and autobiography.

questions.question: Epic poems are a special form of?
questions.explanation: Non-fiction can take the form of poetry — epic poems.

questions.question: Historical plays are a special form of?
questions.explanation: Non-fiction can take the form of drama — historical plays.

questions.question: Prose has the narrative character of ordinary?
questions.explanation: Prose has the narrative character of ordinary storytelling.

questions.question: Prose is described as the youngest of the three genres but the most?
questions.explanation: Prose is the youngest of the three genres but the most popular.

questions.question: Prose may be in oral or in?
questions.explanation: A prose work may be in oral or in written form.

questions.question: Folktales, tongue twisters, myths and legends are all forms of?
questions.explanation: In oral form, folktales, tongue twisters, myths and legends are all forms of prose.

questions.question: Abrams and Harpham describe prose as an inclusive term for all discourse spoken or written which is not patterned into lines of metric?
questions.explanation: Prose is not patterned into lines either of metric verse or non-metric types of discourse.

questions.question: Prose has its greatest strength in attention to details which guarantees the accommodation of vast?
questions.explanation: Prose has its greatest strength in attention to details which guarantees the accommodation of vast literary technique.

questions.question: A short story makes a single impression on the?
questions.explanation: A short story makes a single impression on the reader by concentrating on a single crisis.

questions.question: A short story makes its crisis pivotal in a controlled?
questions.explanation: A short story makes that crisis pivotal in a controlled plot.

questions.question: The style of a short story is compressed and makes use of symbolic language to achieve immediate?
questions.explanation: The style of a short story is compressed and makes use of symbolic language to achieve immediate effect.

questions.question: A good short story does not teach but?
questions.explanation: A good short story does not teach but reveals; it does not preach but interprets.

questions.question: The novel is believed to have grown from African tales, fables, epigrams and?
questions.explanation: In Africa, the novel is believed to have grown from African tales, fables, epigrams, proverbs etc.

questions.question: According to Onuekwusi, the novel rose in the 17th and 18th centuries even in?
questions.explanation: Onuekwusi observes that the novel rose in the 17th and 18th centuries even in Europe.

questions.question: Fantasy is not valid in a?
questions.explanation: Fantasy is not valid in a novel; it bears realistic stories of human beings in real society.

questions.question: The characters in a novel are not strange or inactive but develop as human beings in a?
questions.explanation: The characters in a novel develop as human beings in a physical life.

questions.question: According to Holman, a novel is used in its broadest sense to designate any extended fictional prose?
questions.explanation: Holman asserts that novel designates any extended fictional prose narrative.

questions.question: The actual rise of the novel was the footmark made in Italy around the?
questions.explanation: The actual rise of the novel was the footmark made in Italy around the 13th century.

questions.question: The first English novel was Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe published in?
questions.explanation: Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe was published in 1719 as the first English novel.

questions.question: Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels was another significant early?
questions.explanation: Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels was another significant early work.

questions.question: According to Holman, biography is the accurate presentation of life history from?
questions.explanation: Biography is the accurate presentation of life history from birth to death of an individual.

questions.question: Biography is better referred to as a?
questions.explanation: Biography is better referred to as a life and times book.

questions.question: A biographer writes with the technique of literature and imaginative powers of?
questions.explanation: A biographer writes with the technique of literature and imaginative powers of sublimity.

questions.question: An autobiography contains a person's life and times but written by the person?
questions.explanation: An autobiography contains a person's life and times but written by the person himself.

questions.question: Chinua Achebe's There was a Country is an example of an?
questions.explanation: Chinua Achebe's There was a Country is an example of an autobiography.

questions.question: A novella is normally longer than a short story but shorter than an average?
questions.explanation: A novella is normally longer than a short story but shorter than an average novel.

questions.question: The novella developed from Italy in the?
questions.explanation: The novella developed from Italy in the 14th century.

questions.question: Joseph Conrad's Heart of Darkness is a typical example of a?
questions.explanation: Joseph Conrad's Heart of Darkness is a typical example of a novella.

questions.question: A picaresque novel is both episodic and?
questions.explanation: A picaresque novel is both episodic and satirical in nature.

questions.question: An epistolary novel takes the nature of exchange of?
questions.explanation: An epistolary novel takes the nature of exchange of letters, emails and SMS exchanges.

questions.question: A bildungsroman traces a child's major aspect of growing up and maturation psychologically, socially and?
questions.explanation: A bildungsroman traces a child's growing up and maturation psychologically, socially and spiritually.

questions.question: A sociological novel traces the influence of socioeconomic background of people in a given society at a given?
questions.explanation: A sociological novel traces the influence of socioeconomic background of people at a given period of time.

questions.question: A gothic novel is a narration on antics of ghosts and other horrible incidences that evoke fear and?
questions.explanation: A gothic novel evokes fear and terror through antics of ghosts and horrible incidences.

questions.question: A utopian novel embodies a perfect world where everything goes well without conflicts or?
questions.explanation: A utopian novel embodies a perfect world where everything goes well without conflicts or suffering.

questions.question: George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-four is an example of a?
questions.explanation: George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-four is an example of a dystopian novel.

questions.question: A memoir centres not on the writer's life but on the people and events that?
questions.explanation: A memoir centres not on the writer's life but on the people and events that surround the person.

questions.question: Holman defines diary as a day by day chronicle of?
questions.explanation: Holman defines diary as a day by day chronicle of events kept by an individual.

questions.question: A journal keeps the records of experiences and?
questions.explanation: A journal keeps the records of experiences and thoughts.
